title: Polyclient bootloader playflow — notes & mini-manifest (draft)
summary: Working notes for a small-form installer + sample-app bundler (the "bootloader") that gives new devs a 5–10 minute success path across JS/Python/Go while ramping telemetry and guardrails. Goal is an opinionated, minimal artefact we can iterate on in SDK onboarding labs. This doc is a sketch: experiments, success metrics, example flows, and a checklist for a 2-sprint MVP.
target_personas:
- New backend/frontend engineer evaluating Redwood SDKs for the first time
- Solutions engineer running a 30-minute demo
- Internal engineer spinning a prototype who needs sample app + low-friction creds
goals:
- 1-click local sample app + polyglot client wiring
- Explicit fallback guidance for network/region/permission errors
- Lightweight telemetry (opt-in) that surfaces first-run pain points
- Templates that map to common product patterns (chat, summarization, embeddings)
minimal_success_criteria:
- Fresh user can get a sample convo or embedding call in <=10 minutes on mac/linux/windows with README + CLI
- Telemetry captures install OS, language, flow taken, and first error with anonymized fingerprint
- Two sample apps: chat (JS/React) and document search (Python) working end-to-end
experiment_matrix:
Rows: language (JS, Py, Go), onboarding path (CLI bootloader, raw README, GitHub template), telemetry level (none, minimal, debug), sample app type (chat, embed/search).
Metrics: time-to-first-success, % opt-in telemetry, first-error types, self-serve conversion (signup->API-key created). Prioritize experiments that reduce time-to-success by >=30%.
install_flow_outline:
1) Preflight: check OS, node/python versions, network access (port 443).
2) Offer: choose path (quick-run CLI vs manual).
3) Quick-run: download minimal project (zip or gh template), run 'redwood boot start' which: creates .redwoodrc local with ephemeral dev key prompt, starts sample server, opens a browser demo.
4) Manual: show exact steps for installing client lib, exporting REDWOOD_API_KEY, run minimal snippet.
5) Post-run: in-CLI prompt to open telemetry opt-in and file a feedback note.
Notes: avoid long global installs; use a tiny npm/pip shim that proxies to local execution to keep global footprint low.
telemetry_contract:
- Minimal by default, explicit opt-in prompt post-success.
- Events: install_start, install_complete, sample_run, sample_error (error_code, stage), language, os_family, flow_choice, experiment_bucket.
- No user PII. API keys hashed client-side before sending.
- Stored in internal analytics with retention 60d for onboarding debug, linked to anonymous id.
- CLI exposes 'redwood boot privacy' to show payload and opt-out at any time.
failure_modes_and_mitigation:
- Missing API key: present a fake-mode local simulator and clear next steps to generate a key.
- Network blocked: detect proxy and show curl example + direction to set REDWOOD_PROXY.
- Mismatched model/region: auto-select nearest compatible model variant and surface decision in logs.
- Long cold-start: show expected time and provide a 'dry-run' stub response to keep user engaged.
- Dependency failures: vendor a single-file shim that avoids heavy install pain on first-run.
handoff_notes:
- Engineering: runnable GH template + tiny CLI package; include integration test that validates 'redwood boot start' finishes in <2 minutes in CI.
- Docs: one-page quickstart for 10-minute path + expanded troubleshooting section.
- Solutions: canned demo script for 5–7 minute customer walk-through and FAQs for common permission/network issues.
- SRE: telemetry schema and retention policy, plus a debug endpoint for ephemeral keys used in demos.
open_questions:
- Do we allow auto-creation of ephemeral API keys via console API for new users or require manual console creation?
- Which languages beyond JS/Py/Go get first-class templates (Rust? Java?) and what's the cost of maintenance?
- How aggressive should the CLI be in modifying local files (.gitignore, .env)? Prompting vs auto-change tradeoffs.
- Should the bootloader include a minimal local simulator for offline demos, or is that scope creep?
